newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-PANKRATOV BLOWS CHANCE OF WORLD RECORD.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-PANKRATOV BLOWS CHANCE OF WORLD RECORD.

text.p: Russia's double Olympic champion Denis Pankratov blew his chances of a second short-course world record in consecutive days with a false start in the heats of a World Cup meeting on Sunday.
Pankratov set a world record for the 200 butterfly on the first day of the meeting on Saturday and looked capable of smashing the mark for the 100 race in the discipline.

But the Russian, who was deprived of two world records in Paris last season because of an organisational blunder, was judged to have taken off from his blocks too early in what should have been a straightforward 100 heat and was disqualified.

The mistake could turn out to be costly. In addition to the $2,000 bonus swimmers earn for a world record on the World Cup circuit, Pankratov had a chance of winning a car at the Gelsenkirchen meeting.

The car is handed out to the best performance of the two-day event and a second world record would almost certainly have clinched it. But Pankratov took the mistake in his stride and was happy to laugh with reporters afterwards.
"I wanted to swim quickly this morning and I was just unlucky," he said.
Apart from Saturday, Pankratov seems to have had little luck with his record-breaking attempts in the 25-metre pool.
Almost exactly a year ago Pankratov's world records in the 100 and 200 metres butterfly at a meeting in Paris were not recognised because organisers failed to carry out drug tests.
But the Russian on Saturday clocked one minute 52.64 seconds in the 200 event to beat the previous best of 1:53.05 set by France's Franc Esposito in Paris in February 1994.
There were some fast times in the Sunday morning session of heats. Russian Nina Zhyvanevskaja set a European record for the women's 100 backstroke when she clocked 58.99 seconds.
The finals take place later on Sunday (1400 GMT).
